# Diona
## General information
Their plant-like metabolisms mean they get hungry slower than other species do, but get thirsty faster.
Their "blood" is just sap, and therefore isn't replenished when metabolizing iron.
They take [color=#1e90ff]30% less Blunt damage[/color] and [color=#1e90ff]20% less Slash damage[/color], but [color=#ffa500]50% more Heat damage[/color] and [color=#ffa500]20% more Shock damage[/color]. Their bark-like skin can [color=#ffa500]easily catch fire[/color] when receiving enough Heat damage from [bold]any[/bold] source.[/color]
## Rooting
Diona move around using a dense network of roots. This prevents them from wearing [italic]any[/italic] footwear, but these roots also allow a diona to firmly root themselves to the ground.
While rooted, a diona [color=#ffa500]moves 20% slower[/color], but is able to freely move around in zero-gravity environments instead of awkwardly floating around. Being rooted also causes a diona to passively absorb reagents from puddles they're standing in; this can potentially be dangerous if they're standing in something unsafe to drink!
## Botanical reagents
While diona can digest the same foods that most other species can, they're also affected by certain botanical reagents. Fertilizers will sate their hunger, but pesticides will poison them!
Robust harvest (an especially potent fertilizer) will heal a diona's injuries, but overdosing will cause them to grow out of control, turning into an immobile tree (and dropping all their equipment). Cutting down the tree will "restore" the Diona to their regular, mobile state.
## Diona nymphs
After death, a Diona can voluntarily destroy their own body, releasing their internal organs as three "nymphs", with the player taking control of the nymph containing the brain. The brain nymph can speak, but has no hands or inventory.
After 10 minutes, the brain nymph can regrow into a "full" Diona. This will be a brand-new body with a randomized name, appearance, fingerprints, and even DNA, leaving little evidence beyond their word about who they were before.
